Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; David Kim, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Emma Lopez, Chief Innovation Officer; Tom Reynolds, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover eight key aspects: overall company performance highlights; promotional strategy and effectiveness; marketing campaign effectiveness; pricing actions taken and their impact on sales; price elasticity observations; key strategic priorities and progress; new product launches and innovation pipeline update; and summary of financial results and outlook.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $15.2 billion, representing a 4.2% increase on a reported basis and 5.1% organically compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 52.3%, driven by disciplined pricing, productivity savings, and moderating input costs. Operating income was $2.8 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.45. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me expand on our overall company performance highlights. Despite persistent inflationary pressures on commodities like cocoa, palm oil, and energy—up 15-20% year-over-year in key inputs—and softer category volumes in parts of the portfolio, we delivered strong results, exceeding our guidance on both top- and bottom-line metrics. Net sales reached $15.2 billion, up 4.2% year-over-year, with 4.1% organic sales growth—our strongest in two years—comprising 1.2% volume/mix and 2.9% pricing. Excluding a 1.5% foreign exchange tailwind and 0.6% from our recent acquisition of premium skincare brand Lumina Essentials, core performance was robust. On a two-year stacked basis, organic growth is 9.8%, outpacing the Nielsen-measured CPG industry average of 3.2%.

Net pricing realization of 2.9% reflects disciplined execution. In North American laundry detergents, where we've premiumized our UltraClean pods, we captured 3.5% pricing while growing market share to 28.1%, up 110 basis points per IRI data. Volumes held steady, buoyed by household penetration gains from DTC campaigns. In snacks, pricing was 2.1% amid competition from Frito-Lay expansions, but we offset with 2.3% volume growth via low-sodium baked chips, which saw 25% velocity uplift in test markets.

We gained or held share in 82% of our $25 billion+ measured markets globally, per Kantar and Circana. This shines in beauty and personal care, where share expanded 1.4 points to 22.7%, fueled by e-commerce acceleration.

Adjusted gross margin expanded 210 basis points to 46.2%, the highest in five quarters. This came from $250 million in supply chain productivity, delivering 3.5% manufacturing savings through AI-optimized blending in beverage plants and regenerative agriculture for 40% of coffee volume, reducing cocoa costs by 8%. Freight efficiencies from our hub-and-spoke network added 1.2 points, plus SKU rationalization eliminating 15% of low-velocity items.

Adjusted operating income rose 11.4% to $850 million, with margins up 110 basis points to 17.7%. SG&A declined 40 basis points to 19.0%, driven by zero-based budgeting and our GenAI demand sensing platform, improving forecast accuracy to 92% and cutting inventory obsolescence by 22%. Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.42, up 12.8%, beating guide by 5%. Operating cash flow was $1.1 billion, up 18%, supporting $450 million in repurchases and a dividend hike to $0.48 per share—our 27th consecutive raise.

Regionally, North America grew 4.5% organically, led by health & wellness like probiotic yogurt up 18%. EMEA delivered 3.8% despite category contraction, with premium ice cream up 6%. Latin America surged 12%, and Asia-Pacific was 2.1% with share gains in India.

These results underscore our 'Premiumize, Digitize, Sustain' framework. Premiumization drove 60% of growth, e-commerce hit 18% of sales up from 12%, and recycled PET covers 65% of beverages, reducing Scope 3 emissions 14%.

Now, turning to our promotional strategy and effectiveness—a critical lever amid inflation, shifting behaviors, and competition from private labels like Aldi and Lidl. Our approach is disciplined, data-driven, focused on superior ROI while protecting margins and penetration.

In Q3, we allocated $1.2 billion to trade promotions, 18% of gross sales—up 2% YoY but flat as a percentage due to optimization. Weighted 45% to core SKUs like Crunchy Bites snacks and Zest Energy beverages, 30% to innovations like plant-based Zest Zero Sugar, 25% to back-to-school and holiday events. Average ROI improved to 3.8x from 3.4x, ahead of our 3.5x target, via 12% reduction in unproductive overlap using our AI pricing engine.

Effectiveness metrics: 17% sales lift on promoted items per Nielsen IRI, 92% ACV distribution, 4% EBV growth. Coupon redemptions at 2.8% via Zest Rewards app (15 million active U.S. households), 25% repeat uplift. Funded displays at 4.2x ROI, capturing 1.2 snack share points vs. Frito-Lay.

North America (55% budget) outperformed at -2.8 elasticity, EDLP hybrid with Target yielding 22% Zest lift. Europe (25%) at 3.5x despite HFSS regs, UK Tesco partnership 19% NMV growth. APAC (15%) strongest at 4.1x, China Tmall 28% lift.

Tech boosts: Prometheus AI forecasts lift store-SKU-week, 22% error reduction; blockchain cuts fraud 8%; zero-based planning scaled 40% pilots.

Adapting to right-shifting, value-engineered promos like BOGO 50% on Zest. Q4: $1.3 billion spend, 4.0x ROI target.

Next, our pricing actions and their impact on sales. Amid 6-8% input inflation like cocoa and PET, we executed disciplined strategy, protecting margins without losing share.

Net pricing +5.2% YoY, up from 4.1% Q2. Net sales +3.8% reported, 4.2% organic: +5.2% pricing, -1.0% volume/mix. Outpacing CPG's 2.1%.

Snacks: +6.8%, 8-10% list hikes on CrunchMax and ZestBar, flat volume, +1.5% premium mix, +10 bps share. Beverages: +4.7%, 6% hikes, -2.1% volume offset by functional lines. Health & Beauty: +4.1%, premiumization +2.3% mix.

North America +5.6%, good-better-best tiering. Europe +3.9%, volume terms. Emerging +6.8%, sachet innovations.

'Value over Volume' via VoC panel, elasticity -0.9. Q4 +4.5-5.0% pricing.

On price elasticity observations: Aggregate coefficient -0.85, improved from -1.12 YoY, firmly inelastic. Beverages -1.42 volatile, snacks -0.72 resilient, household -0.58 necessity-driven.

North America -0.92, Europe -0.76, emerging -1.05. Pricing AI with Palantir forecasts 92% accuracy, dynamic pilots reduce deep discounts 35%.

Prioritizing power brands with <-0.8 elasticity.

Now, our summary of financial results and outlook. Net sales $15.2B, +4.2% reported, 5.1% organic: 2.8% pricing, 1.7% mix, 0.6% volume. Gross margin +120 bps to 52.3% from pricing, easing costs, $150M productivity. Operating income +6.5% to $2.8B, EPS $1.45 +8%.

Snacks 7.2% organic, beverages 3.8%, personal care +0.9%, household +4.5%. North America 6.1%, EMEA 1.8%, APAC 9.2%, LATAM 3.4%.

Q4 organic 4-5%, gross +50-75 bps, EPS $1.52-1.56. FY24 tightened: organic +4.5-5%, op margin 18.3-18.5%, EPS $5.95-6.05.

Next, Lisa will provide insights on our marketing and brand initiatives.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Our brand building efforts, including marketing campaign effectiveness, have contributed significantly to our performance. We are seeing strong engagement across channels, especially with our new Summer Surge campaign.

We allocated 12.8% of net sales to marketing, up 50 bps YoY. Blended ROAS 4.7x, +18% YoY, outperforming peers via MMM with NielsenIQ/IRI.

Summer Surge for PeakPure lemonades: $145M incremental from $28M spend, 5.2x ROAS, 14% grocery velocity, +7 pts Gen Z penetration. Clean Slate for FreshGlow: 3.9x ROAS, +2.2 share in natural channels, 6.1x in APAC e-comm.

Digital 68% budget, CTV 7.2x. Privacy Sandbox preserves 85% signals, clean rooms cut CAC to $4.20. AI creative +27% CTR.

North America 5.3x, LatAm 4.9x, EMEA 3.4x. Prioritizing CLV +12% to $142, Q4 DTC to 25% spend, 5.0x+ ROAS.

Following me, David will discuss supply chain performance.

David Kim:
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to optimize our supply chain network and implement advanced technologies to improve efficiency and resilience. We are also focused on reducing our carbon footprint, tying into our key strategic priorities and progress.

Our strategy anchors on portfolio premiumization, sustainable innovation, and digital omnichannel acceleration. Power Brands 75% portfolio, premium grew 12% organic, +200 bps margin to 48.2%. Divested low-margin soups for $400M cash.

VitalFit bars +1.8 share, EcoGlow 18% uplift. Sustainable: 95% recycled content goal early, 35% sales sustainable +300 bps growth. E-comm 28%, DTC +35%, AI personalization.

Supply chain: S&OP AI cut inventory 15% to 8.2 weeks, $120M WC savings, on track $300M productivity.

After me, Emma will share updates on our product innovation pipeline.

Emma Lopez:
Thank you, David. We are excited about our pipeline of innovative products. Our recent product launch, VitaGlow Plant-Powered Protein Shakes, has been well-received, generating $28M sales ahead of plan, 65% ACV.

CrunchNova Veggie Crisps $15M, 35% repeat. EcoShield $12M, +0.8 share. 2024 launches +28% ahead, 15 SKUs.

Pipeline: 45 projects, $450M R&D. Q3 HydroBev, Q4 RenewFiber. Mid-term: CreamWave milk, SkinSync serums.

Tailored regionally, four pillars: speed, sustainability, tech, discipline. Expect 15-18% 2025 revenue from new products.

Finally, Tom will discuss our sales performance and channel strategy.

Tom Reynolds:
Thank you, Emma. We are focused on expanding our distribution channels and improving sales execution. We are seeing strong growth in our e-commerce channel, now 18%, and investing in retail partnerships like Walmart and Kroger, with 98.7% ACV in snacks.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions as before. Our first question comes from Jamie Carter with Goldman Sachs.

Jamie Carter:
How is your company addressing the increasing demand for sustainable products?

Emma Lopez:
Great question, Jamie. Sustainability is core to our innovation, with 35% of sales now from sustainable products, up from 25%, contributing 300 bps to growth. We've hit 95% recycled content early, like GreenEarth pods with 10% velocity boost, and pipeline like RenewFiber pods zero microplastics. In APAC, eco-personal care up 22%, aligned with regs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Lee with JPMorgan.

Rachel Lee:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Tom Reynolds:
Thanks, Rachel. Emerging markets are key, 22% mix, with +6.8% pricing and 1.5% volume. APAC up 9.2%, India/Indonesia via sachets and modern trade +3 pts ACV. LATAM 12% surge, Brazil local production. We'll leverage omnichannel, e-comm 18% global, tailored innovations like yuzu CrunchNova in Japan.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mark Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Mark Patel:
Can you discuss the impact of inflation on your pricing strategy and consumer demand?

Michael Chen:
Sure, Mark. Inflation at 6-8% on inputs prompted +5.2% net pricing, driving organic growth while elasticity improved to -0.85 inelastic. Volumes -1.0% but mix +1.7%, share gains as consumers stick to brands. Productivity $150M offsets, margins +120 bps. Q4 +4.5-5.0% pricing amid cooling inflation.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays.

Sarah Kim:
How are you leveraging artificial intelligence to improve your supply chain efficiency?

David Kim:
Excellent point, Sarah. AI is transformative: Prometheus for promo forecasting, 22% error cut; S&OP for 15% inventory reduction, 98% service; GenAI demand sensing 92% accuracy. Pricing AI dynamic pilots, trade opti $300M spend at 4.5x ROI. Piloting robotized DCs for 20% labor gains.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to deliver long-term sustainable growth and create value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the GCB Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
